cells.tense: This is here now, and this person is meeting it while the door is still open.
cells.ask: Take one thing that arrived this week and give it a shape today — a time, a place, or one small step for it.
cells.core: Something is coming in, and the person here is handling it as it comes. That is the whole position. The strength that builds is working the way it should: not straining ahead, not hanging back, just giving form to what shows up. In the middle of an ordinary day this is already happening. A problem gets a time set for it. A date gets written down. A thing that needs doing gets a first move. What arrives is received on purpose instead of piling up unhandled.\n\nThe other side of this is staying in touch with what is actually in front of them while they hold the line on something. The person in front of them still gets through. The feeling in the room still gets through. One way to keep that alive is to say out loud what just came in, even if it is small. Naming it counts as meeting it.
cells.sheetLine: What arrives gets a shape from this person, on purpose.
cells.verb: meeting what lands and giving it shape
cells.place: the threshold where what arrives comes in

cells.tense: They are building for a future that has not arrived, readying the door before it opens.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are preparing for and leave its next step unplanned until tomorrow.
cells.core: The strength to meet what comes is running ahead of what is here. Something might arrive, and a plan is being built for it before it has shown up — a version of the future getting nailed down while the present waits. The building is real, the strength is real, and it is aimed at something that has not happened yet. Bracing takes the place of receiving. The same grip that holds something together is holding a future that cannot be written yet.\n\nUnderneath, the fear is usually that if it is not built in advance, it will land too hard. So the question becomes what is actually fair to what is coming. Fair means letting it have its own timing. Let one thing arrive tomorrow without having been built for today, and the strength gets something real to meet instead of something feared.

cells.tense: They are still standing at a door that is already behind them, holding what is finished.
cells.ask: Name out loud that one thing is done, then close it — put it away, mark it finished, tell one person it is over.
cells.core: The strength to meet what is arriving is there, but it is not being used at the threshold. Attention is still on something that already came in, and that attention has taken the place of receiving anything new. A finish has not been called, so the hands stay full of what is done. The person is here in the body, present, while the grip is on something that ended. Giving it an ending is part of giving it a shape.\n\nNothing needs to be pushed toward feeling here, and nothing needs to be forced open. What is needed is one completed thing, named as finished, out in the open where it can be seen. When something is truly called done, the hands come free for what is waiting outside. What has been standing there gets its chance to come in.
cells.sheetLine: They are at the threshold but still holding what already came through.
cells.verb: meeting what lands and giving it shape
cells.place: the threshold where what arrives comes in

cells.tense: This person is already giving shape to what arrives, and speaking as though it happens on its own.
cells.ask: Once today, catch something you shaped and say 'I did that' — name it as yours out loud, even to yourself.
cells.core: The shaping is already underway. What arrives gets met and given form — a time, a place, a way to proceed — and then the telling makes it sound as though it fell into place by itself. People around this person can see the shape and can feel the evenness of it, while the one doing the work keeps quiet about doing it. There is freshness in it too, because each thing that arrives makes its own demand.\n\nClaiming it takes one sentence, no speech. Say plainly that this thing has a shape because you gave it one. That is the whole move. When the claim catches up to what is already happening, the work gets its own name attached to it, and the person who did it gets to keep what they made.
cells.sheetLine: The shaping is already happening, and this person has not said it is theirs.
